messages.subject: local minimum
parts:
Hi,

I am running IRACE on a non-deterministic algorithm with the exact same conditions as the real algorithm (number of instances, number of iteration, ext.)

Unfortunately, the elite configurations I got is not accurate and the final results are worse than the manual configurations.
I know that the problems which the algorithm trying to solve have many local minima and I think that this might be the problem.
In most case, all the elite configurations are very similar to each other and might represented the same local minimum.

Do you have any suggestion to deal with such case? any ways to eviod the local minimum?


thank you!
Naama

messages.author: 854a0709976c2a48
messages.subject: Re: local minimum
parts:
Hi Naama,

irace is designed to converge quickly so it is not surprising that it gets stuck on local optima. The restart mechanism should ideally help early stagnation. Look in the output of irace if restarts are being triggered. If not, then analyze why not (typical reason is that numerical values are different enough to not trigger it, you could play with digits to reduce the resolution of numerical parameters).

You will have to analyze a bit the output of irace to understand why irace is not finding the best possible solutions. But there are quite a few things to try:

* If the variance across instances/runs is high, then irace may miss the best configuration if the best was unlucky on a few runs. You could try increasing firstTest.
* If you are providing the manual configuration as a starting solution, and the final configuration is similar to the manual one, this may be biasing the search too strongly. You may wish to remove this and then perform more independent runs of irace with smaller budgets using different seeds for each run of irace.

* If you are providing the manual configuration as a starting solution, but it gets eliminated, then irace does not think it is good. You need to investigate why this happens.

* On the other hand, if you are not providing the manual configuration to irace, maybe you should to direct irace towards a good area of the search space.

* Make sure that the way you decide that the manual configuration is better is also the way that irace compares configurations. Otherwise, irace is not optimizing the same thing as you do.

* "better" must be statistically better. That is, the manual conf may have smaller mean, but the t-test used by irace may say that the difference is not significant, thus it is not actually better.

* If you define "better" on the test set, be sure that the manual configuration was not tuned for the test set. irace uses a different training set, so it doesn't overfit. It may be a good idea to compare manual and irace on a different sample of instances from the same problem, just to be sure that manual is indeed better.

Cheers,

Manuel.
